issue.title: Add aria-label to the booking page duration badge
issue.body: Harness test (simple change). In apps/web/modules/bookings/components/event-meta/Duration.tsx, give the duration text an accessible label like "Duration: 30 minutes" (localized, English key in packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json) without changing the visible text. Include a unit test.

pm.summary: Small UI change: give every duration shown on the booking page a localized screen-reader label like "Duration: 30 minutes", keep the visible text the same, and add a unit test. Ready for implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Single-duration event (no multiple durations, not dynamic): the duration text on the booking page has an accessible name of the form "Duration: <duration>", e.g. a 30-minute event exposes "Duration: 30 minutes".
Multiple-duration event with the duration selector hidden: the selected (or default) duration text has the same kind of accessible label, matching the duration shown.

Multiple-duration or dynamic event with the selector visible: each duration option has its own accessible label with its duration (e.g. the 15 option reads "Duration: 15 minutes"), and the selected and clickable behavior is unchanged.

Durations of 60 minutes or more, e.g. 90, get a label that a screen reader can understand and that matches the visible value (hours and minutes). The label must not be the short visible form such as "1h 30m".
The visible text is the same as before for all paths (e.g. "30m", "1h 30m"). No layout or styling changes.
The label text comes from i18n. A new English key is added to packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json, and no user-facing label string is hardcoded in the component.
Other places that use getDurationFormatted, such as BookFormAsModal, show the same output as before.

A unit test inside apps/web/ renders the duration component and checks the accessible label for at least the single-duration case and one multiple-duration option. It also checks that the visible text is unchanged. The test passes.

research.summary: Research is done. Duration.tsx shows the duration in three places, two of them bare fragments with no element to carry a label, and existing pluralized i18n keys can produce the long form. Next: planning.
patterns: Duration.tsx has three render paths. Line 93 (single duration) and line 101 (hidden selector) return a bare fragment `<>{getDurationFormatted(...)}</>`, so there is no element to put an aria-label on. Line 131 (multiple durations or a dynamic event, selector visible) renders `<li data-testId=multiple-choice-${duration}mins data-active ... onClick>` with an inner `<div className="w-max">`.

getDurationFormatted(mins, t) at Duration.tsx:14 builds the short visible form from the keys minute_one_short ("{{count}}m"), hour_one_short ("{{count}}h") and multiple_duration_timeUnit_short. It is also imported by BookFormAsModal.tsx:68, so changing what it returns would change the modal's output.

Existing pluralized long-form keys in en/common.json can build a readable label without a new formatter key: minute_one/minute_other ("{{count}} minute(s)", lines 1805-1807) and hour_one/hour_other (lines 1808-1810), called as t("minute", { count }) or t("hour", { count }). "duration": "Duration" already exists at line 920. Duration keys sit around lines 920-927 (duration, multiple_duration_*). The en file has no existing *_aria_label key to follow for naming.
EventDuration is rendered by Details.tsx:146 inside EventMetaBlock (icon="clock"). It is the only consumer of the component.

Test infrastructure: the vitest workspace project '@calcom/web/modules/views' picks up apps/web/modules/**/*.{test,spec}.tsx with jsdom and setupFiles apps/web/modules/test-setup.ts. That setup file already mocks @calcom/embed-core/embed-iframe (useIsEmbed: vi.fn()) and mocks useLocale so that t returns the key unchanged. To assert interpolated text like "Duration: 30 minutes", a test needs a local vi.mock of @calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale with a t that interpolates, or it can assert on the key and params.

Store-backed render helper: `render` from @calcom/features/bookings/Booker/__tests__/test-utils accepts { mockStore: Partial<BookerStore> } (selectedDuration, state, setSelectedDuration), as used in DatePicker.test.tsx. Booker.test.tsx shows the vi.mock pattern for @calcom/atoms/hooks/useIsPlatform, which EventDuration also imports. EventDuration also imports useShouldShowArrows from @calcom/web/modules/apps/components/AllApps, a plain hook (refs and state) that may need a mock if the import pulls in heavy dependencies.
Tests live next to their components (e.g. apps/web/modules/bookings/components/DatePicker.test.tsx), so the natural test location is apps/web/modules/bookings/components/event-meta/Duration.test.tsx.
None of the touched files is under a human_review prefix. Both Duration.tsx and en/common.json are within the allowed scope.
No CLAUDE.md or CONTRIBUTING.md in the repo root. Formatting and linting use biome (biome.json at the root; apps/web lint script is `biome lint .`).

design_need.summary: No design needed: this adds screen-reader labels to the existing duration display and changes nothing visible. Next: planning.
